topics.topic: Resolve the undeclared config reference in create_budget_schema
questions: Must the config reference be removed or explicitly declared spec-only, or must an import providing config be added to IMPORTS?
Must the config.persistence reference be removed in favor of the stated fixed table names, or must the required config import be added to IMPORTS?

judgement.why: This is the same fixed-table-name versus config-import question already answered by P1, and the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Decide whether schema SQL names come from imported config constants or are fixed literals
quotes: create_budget_schema: [CONFIG_REFERENCE] MUST idempotently create only the tables budget_versions (= config.persistence.budget_version_table_name) and section_plans (= config.persistence.section_plan_table_name), written as fixed names in the SQL text, with columns corresponding one-to-one to BudgetVersion and SectionPlan fields; version_id and plan_id are primary keys, (version_id, section_id) is unique, and nullable model fields remain nullable.
Use only the IMPORTS listed above plus required standard library imports.
precedent.why: The prompt explicitly requires the literal fixed table names in SQL and permits no unlisted config-module import.

topics.topic: Resolve the conflicting connection parameter annotation requirements
questions: Must connection retain the contractually required object annotation, or must the prohibition on object annotations change?
Must connection retain the contractually required object annotation, or must the prohibition on object annotations change?

quotes: def __init__(self, connection: object, context: AuditRepositoryContext) -> None
Import from IMPORTS every symbol the module uses, including symbols used only in annotations, and annotate each parameter with the type its CONTRACTS signature declares, never object or nothing.
judgement.why: The declared signatures require object for both connection parameters, while the later instruction forbids annotating any parameter as object.

topics.topic: Whether to escape whitespace and control characters in path values to preserve the four-field log record format
questions: Must path whitespace and control characters be escaped to preserve the four-field, single-space-delimited record format, or must they remain unchanged even though they can introduce additional separators or record lines?

Must path values be escaped so the record always contains exactly four single-space-separated fields, or must path characters remain unchanged even when they introduce additional whitespace or line boundaries?

quotes: MUST return exactly four labelled fields, each written as label=value and separated by single spaces, in the order rid (the request id), method, path and status, so an operator log parser does not change between builds.

The path value is the canonical_path argument exactly as given, which the caller already took from _canonical_path over the request path without its query string: the function MUST NOT truncate, shorten, escape, encode, redact or otherwise inspect it, so the ids a route path carries appear in the record as they are, and a control character such as a newline that the server decoded into the path is written unchanged.
judgement.why: The requirement to preserve an exact four-field, single-space-separated record conflicts with the requirement to leave path whitespace and control characters unchanged.
